analysis:
The changes are documentation-only: a date bump in docs/developer/test.md, a new test command at head line 998 (scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py), a descriptive paragraph at head lines 1024-1031, and a note in docs/operations/provider-release.md around line 196. The note says that only pull-request runs may use Darkbloom Sandboxes under CI runner routing, and that master and dispatched runs always use literal Blacksmith runners. No runtime code, protocol, key handling, cache storage or attestation logic changes, so no change lands on assets A-001 to A-017 or on the TB-002/003/007/009/010/011 boundaries.

The text describes a CI routing control: default-off switch, fork PR refusal, exact label grants, an untrusted or plain-HTTP plane being refused, and hostile reply text. It also states that release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners, and that routed jobs have a pinned fallback, a timeout and read-only permissions. This reads as a security-positive description. The routing script, workflow files and build.md#ci-runner-routing are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm the documented behaviour matches the implementation. In particular, the claims that release/signing workflows are isolated from routed runners, that fork PRs cannot reach the plane, and that the read-only permissions hold are unverified here. That is a coverage limit, not a finding. The claim in provider-release.md that the signing-free cache jobs run only on Blacksmith for master and dispatched runs is consistent with the existing statement that those jobs hold no signing or publication secrets. The remaining test.md excerpts are unchanged context and carry no new claims. T-041 and the other retained cache threats are unaffected.

The next pass should check the actual workflow and routing script if they appear in another batch.
